memory_update.text: AXTI should remain a priority Layer 2 diligence candidate for the optical_transceiver_substrates node because Q1 2026 InP revenue, backlog, and capacity-expansion language directly map to the hypothesized substrate chokepoint.
VECO is a high-quality second-order candidate: not a substrate owner, but equipment orders for InP laser manufacturing can validate the upstream capacity expansion cycle.

AAOI and COHR should be used as reference demand/technology anchors, not as the main underfollowed discovery lane; their 1.6T order and product data help test whether InP substrate demand is structural.

Next pass should verify AXTI customer identities indirectly through export-permit geography, top-five customer trends, purchase commitments, and cross-read from Lumentum, Coherent, AAOI, Semtech and Asian transceiver makers.

node: Precision substrates and components for 800G/1.6T AI optical transceivers
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the narrow optical-transceiver substrate/component node. The strongest underfollowed direct candidate is AXT Inc. because its indium phosphide substrate revenue and backlog are now explicitly tied to data-center demand. Veeco is a second-order equipment bottleneck for InP laser manufacturing. Applied Optoelectronics is a direct module-level customer/volume-ramp anchor. Coherent is the obvious large-cap reference leader across lasers, photonic components, ICs and transceivers. This is research support only, not a buy/sell list.
